items.stem: Why should vulnerability findings be prioritised using more than the raw CVSS score?

options.text: Exposure, exploitability and business context change the real risk
options.rationale: Correct: context determines which high-severity items matter most.
CVSS is useful; it is simply not the whole picture.

options.text: Prioritisation is unnecessary if you have a scanner
options.rationale: A scanner finds issues; prioritisation decides what to fix first.

options.text: Only the newest findings ever matter
options.rationale: Age alone does not determine priority.

items.explanation: Correct: exposure, exploitability and business context refine raw severity.

items.stem: Which TWO practices strengthen a remediation workflow? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Assigning each finding an owner and a deadline
options.rationale: Correct: clear ownership and deadlines drive timely fixes.

options.text: Verifying fixes with a targeted rescan
options.rationale: Correct: rescanning confirms the vulnerability is actually resolved.

options.text: Closing findings as fixed without checking
options.rationale: Unverified closure leaves real risk open.

options.text: Ignoring findings with no available patch
options.rationale: Mitigations or compensating controls should be applied meanwhile.

items.explanation: Correct: clear ownership/deadlines and verification by rescan both strengthen remediation.

items.stem: What is the main advantage of an authenticated vulnerability scan?

options.text: It can assess configuration and missing patches from the inside, finding more issues
options.rationale: Correct: credentials let the scanner inspect the host in depth.
No scan type guarantees zero false positives.

options.text: It never needs an asset inventory
options.rationale: An inventory is still essential for coverage.

options.text: It replaces the need for remediation
options.rationale: Scanning finds issues; remediation still fixes them.

items.explanation: Correct: authenticated scans inspect the host from the inside and find more.
